title: Decoupling with SQS, SNS, and EventBridge

questions.prompt: In Amazon SQS, how many consumers process each message?
questions.explanation: SQS is a point-to-point queue: each message is delivered to and processed by a single consumer, then deleted.

questions.prompt: You need one event to reach three independent services. Which service fits best?

options.text: Amazon SNS (pub/sub fan-out), often to a queue per service

questions.explanation: SNS publishes to a topic and pushes a copy to every subscriber (fan-out), commonly to a separate SQS queue per service. A single SQS queue would deliver the message to only one consumer.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an SQS standard queue and a FIFO queue?

options.text: Standard has strict ordering; FIFO is unordered
Standard offers high throughput with at-least-once/best-effort order; FIFO guarantees strict order and exactly-once at lower throughput

questions.explanation: Standard queues maximize throughput with at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering; FIFO queues guarantee ordering and exactly-once processing but with lower throughput.

questions.prompt: Which are benefits of decoupling components with messaging? Select all that apply.

options.text: Work waits in the queue if a consumer is temporarily down
Producers and consumers can scale independently
It removes the need for any IAM permissions

questions.explanation: Decoupling adds resilience (work waits), independent scaling, and buffering. It does not remove IAM requirements.

questions.prompt: Messages that repeatedly fail processing can be automatically moved to a ____-letter queue for inspection.
questions.explanation: A dead-letter queue (DLQ) isolates messages that fail repeatedly so they can be examined instead of retrying forever or being lost.

questions.prompt: Match each messaging service to what it's for.

pairs.right: Broadcast one message to many subscribers
Route events to targets by content rules

questions.explanation: SQS buffers point-to-point, SNS fans out pub/sub, EventBridge routes events by rules, and a DLQ isolates failing messages.
